facts.text: Margaret Doyle is the person being assessed.
Priya Nair is a social worker from adult social care.
The assessment is a needs assessment under the Care Act.
The reason for the assessment is to understand how Margaret is managing daily life, what is difficult, what is working, and what matters to her.
Margaret does not want to be placed in a care home or institution.
The assessment is not about placing Margaret in a care home or institution.
The assessment is about Margaret being in her own home and what might make things easier for her.
The assessment will take about an hour.
Margaret has a quiz programme at 4 o'clock that she will be free from.
Margaret was in the kitchen when the fall occurred.
The fall occurred on Monday, the third of March.
Margaret was going to make tea when the fall happened.
Margaret is uncertain whether she tripped or went dizzy.
Margaret fell from the sink to the floor by the back door.
Margaret was on the floor for about two hours.
Margaret could not get up after the fall.
Margaret tried to turn over but could not put any weight on her wrist.
Margaret did not bang her head when she fell.
Margaret was not able to call anyone while on the floor because her phone was in the front room.
Margaret heard her phone ringing at one point but could not get to it.
Margaret was found by Brenda, her neighbour, who noticed the curtains were not drawn and the kitchen light was off.
Brenda had a key and let herself in.
Brenda rang the ambulance and sat on the cold floor holding Margaret's hand until they arrived.
Margaret was taken to St Aldhelm's Hospital.
Margaret stayed in hospital for four days.
Margaret was admitted to the orthopaedic ward.
Margaret fractured her left wrist.
Margaret is left-handed.
Margaret has difficulty with daily tasks such as opening jars and doing buttons due to her wrist injury.
Margaret had bruising on her side, not broken bones in her hips.
Margaret Doyle can walk about ten minutes to the shops before the fall.
Margaret Doyle now feels frightened of walking, even for short distances, after her fall.
Margaret Doyle had a fall in the garden before Christmas, where she sat down on the grass.
Margaret Doyle had a fall in the bathroom in January, where she caught herself on the sink.
Margaret Doyle has had three falls in the last six months, including one in March.
Margaret Doyle did not tell her GP about the two earlier falls.
Margaret Doyle did not tell her doctor about the falls, stating she did not want to bother him.
Margaret Doyle's GP is Dr Shah at Millbrook Surgery, Church Lane.
Margaret Doyle has not been referred to a falls clinic or had a falls assessment by her GP.
The bedroom and bathroom are upstairs, and the only toilet is upstairs.
Margaret Doyle has to go up and down stairs to use the toilet during the day.
Margaret Doyle tries not to drink too much in the afternoons to reduce the need to go to the toilet.
There is a rail on the right side of the stairs when going up.
Margaret Doyle goes up the stairs one at a time, holding on with her right hand.
When coming down the stairs, the rail is on the wrong side for her right hand, so she goes down sideways or on her bottom if tired.
Margaret Doyle sometimes goes down the stairs on her bottom, especially when tired, in private.
There is only one frame, which is left at the bottom and used by holding onto the wall at the top.
Margaret Doyle believes a second rail and a second frame for upstairs would be helpful.
There are several rugs in the hall and in the living room, which were previously owned by Frank's mother.
One rug in the hall was brought back from a holiday in Wales years ago.
The rugs are a trip hazard, especially with the frame.
Kevin Doyle has repeatedly reminded Margaret about the rugs.
Margaret Doyle gets up in the night to use the toilet, sometimes once or twice.
Margaret Doyle leaves the landing light on at night to help with nighttime toilet use.
The bathroom is located right next to the bedroom, only a few steps away.
Margaret Doyle does not currently have a pendant alarm or fall detection device.
Margaret Doyle said she does not want to wear a necklace or pendant, as she does not want to look like an 'old woman'.
Margaret Doyle expressed interest in a wrist-worn fall detection device that can call for help automatically, even if she cannot press a button.
Margaret Doyle said she would be interested in a fall detection device, and agreed to be recorded as interested.
Margaret Doyle currently performs a 'strip wash' at the sink upstairs using a flannel.
Margaret Doyle reports that she sometimes does not make it to the toilet and experiences leakage when she leaves it too long, especially when going upstairs.
Margaret Doyle wears pads at night and purchases them from the supermarket.
Kevin Doyle buys the night pads for Margaret at the big shop.
Margaret Doyle is interested in seeing the continence service, which can assess her and provide free pads if eligible, advice, and exercises.
Margaret Doyle confirms she is happy to receive a referral to the continence service.
Margaret Doyle eats one slice of toast with marmalade and a cup of tea for breakfast.
Margaret Doyle has soup (tin of tomato or chicken) with bread sometimes for lunch or dinner.
Margaret Doyle eats yoghurt and sometimes crackers and cheese in the evening, but finds cutting cheese difficult with one hand.
Margaret Doyle has not cooked since the fall and has not turned the cooker on since coming home.
Margaret Doyle cannot lift pans and does not like being in the kitchen due to fear of falling, which occurred at the sink.
Margaret Doyle used to cook every day and prepare proper dinners, including Sunday roasts with meat and vegetables.
Margaret Doyle lost nearly a stone since Christmas and her clothes are now hanging off her.
Margaret Doyle lost nearly a stone since Christmas, and the hospital nurse was cross about the weight loss.
Margaret Doyle weighs eight stone something and was previously nine and a half stone.
Margaret Doyle's appetite comes and goes and she does not feel hungry like she used to, especially when alone.
Kevin Doyle does a big shop on Sunday when he visits.
Brenda delivers milk and bread to Margaret during the week if she runs out.
Margaret Doyle has a microwave and uses it to cook jacket potatoes sometimes.
Kevin Doyle put ready meals in the freezer, but Margaret cannot remove the film from the top.
Margaret Doyle stabs the film off with a fork, but it goes everywhere.
Margaret Doyle takes amlodipine (5mg, once daily in the morning) for blood pressure.
Margaret Doyle takes alendronic acid (70mg, once weekly on Monday) for bone health, which must be taken with a large glass of water and sitting upright for 30 minutes.
Margaret Doyle takes paracetamol (2 tablets, up to 4 times a day) for wrist pain, but only takes it once or twice a day if needed.
Margaret Doyle missed two doses of her blood pressure tablet last week (Tuesday and Thursday morning), and admitted she is not usually like this.
Margaret Doyle has trouble opening the dosette box flaps with her wrist and uses a butter knife to open it.
Margaret Doyle has a dosette box delivered every Friday by the chemist on Station Road, which has days marked on it.
Margaret Doyle has been short on money recently and is unsure where it has gone, though she believes she is just not keeping track like she used to.
Kevin Doyle has a key to the house and can enter the property.
Kevin Doyle is present during the assessment and is invited to join the discussion.
Kevin Doyle says he has been telling Margaret about the rugs in the house for years.
Kevin Doyle is the son of Margaret Doyle.
Margaret Doyle lives in a house with stairs, a garden, and a back step with a drop.
The light at the top of the stairs is operated by a pull cord, requiring Margaret to reach around to turn it on.
The house has a boiler that was replaced last year.
Kevin Doyle visits Margaret on Sundays, and occasionally midweek if he is on early shifts.
Kevin Doyle commutes from Northampton, which is 40 minutes by car.
Kevin Doyle works shifts at a warehouse.
Kevin Doyle has two teenage children and his wife works.
Margaret has a daughter named Susan who lives in Alicante, Spain.
Susan Doyle (daughter) calls Margaret every week on Sunday nights.
Susan Doyle visits Margaret during the summer months.
Susan Doyle was unable to visit Margaret after her fall due to work commitments.
Kevin Doyle was on the phone with Margaret every day during her fall.
Brenda, who lives next door, visits Margaret most days for a minute.
Brenda knocks on the wall in the morning and Margaret knocks back as a signal to indicate she is well.
Brenda is 76 years old and has knee problems, so Margaret does not lean on her.
Margaret used to attend a lunch club at St Michael's church hall on Wednesdays, but it is now on Thursdays at 12 o'clock.
The lunch club at St Michael's offers a cooked dinner, pudding, and activities such as bingo or quizzes, and sometimes features guest speakers.
At the last lunch club, a man brought real owls, one of which sat on Margaret's arm.
Margaret stopped attending the lunch club after her fall.
Margaret used to walk to the lunch club, which is only a short distance round the corner past shops.
Margaret cannot walk to the lunch club now due to her condition.
Margaret misses the people at the lunch club, specifically Joan and Pat, whom she used to sit with.
Margaret expressed a desire to return to the lunch club if transport is available.
Margaret reports feeling lonely, especially on days when no one visits.
On days when no one visits, Margaret spends long hours watching television and doing word searches.
Margaret cannot hold a pen now and is unable to do word searches.
Margaret has not spoken to anyone except Biscuit and the man on the television during days when no one visits.
Margaret experienced a significant decline in mood after Frank's death in August of the previous year.
Margaret reported being in a 'bad way' after Frank's death, not wanting to get up or eat, and sitting in his chair for weeks.
Margaret Doyle has not smoked for 30 years, stopped when Kevin was young.
Frank (Margaret's husband) continues to smoke.
Margaret reports her memory is generally okay, though she forgets where she has put her glasses.
Margaret can still recall all the kings and queens.
Margaret is concerned about money being withdrawn from her account without her knowledge.
Margaret said she was unsure where the money had gone.
Margaret identified her grandson Jordan as the person who has been borrowing her bank card.
Jordan is 22 years old and lives in town in a flat with his girlfriend.
Jordan visits Margaret occasionally and is described as 'lovely' with her.
Jordan has borrowed Margaret's bank card to get cash for himself or to pay for Margaret's shopping.
Margaret told Jordan the number of her bank card so he could get her shopping when she first came out of hospital.
Margaret's bank statement shows over 600 pounds withdrawn over the last two months, more than she asked Jordan for.
Margaret does not want Jordan to get into trouble, as he is young and has had a hard time with his mother moving to Spain.
Margaret said she does not want to make a fuss about the situation.
Margaret said she does not remember everything she told Jordan about the card.
Jordan currently has Margaret's bank card.
Jordan is expected to return Margaret's bank card on Saturday.
Margaret said she would be happy for Kevin to know about the money issue and for the conversation to happen in front of him.
Margaret said Kevin will have to know because he will be the one sorting it out.
Margaret said she is not comfortable with the police being involved in the situation with Jordan.
Kevin said he is angry with Jordan, not with Margaret.
Kevin said he believes Jordan has his mother's bank card PIN.
Margaret gave Jordan her bank card PIN when she came out of hospital so he could do her shopping.
Kevin said Brenda (a neighbour) told him a few weeks ago that she thought she saw Jordan at a cash machine on the high street, near the chemist.
Kevin said Brenda was not sure it was Jordan and that she doesn't have her glasses on half the time.
Kevin said Brenda once thought she saw the Pope in the Co-op.
Kevin said he heard from one of Jordan's old mates' mothers that Jordan has been gambling on his phone through gambling apps and is in debt.
Margaret said the information about Jordan gambling is 'just gossip' and that Kevin does not know it.
Kevin said he believes Jordan is taking Margaret's pension money and that this is theft.
Kevin said he thinks Jordan should be punished with a 'clip round the ear'.
Margaret Doyle has state pension and receives half of Frank's railway pension as a widow's pension.
The house is owned and paid off years ago.
Margaret has approximately £9,000 in a building society account, designated as funeral money and for grandchildren.
Margaret is not currently receiving Attendance Allowance or other benefits.
Attendance Allowance is a benefit for people over state pension age who need help with personal care, not means-tested, and Margaret may be entitled to it.
Kevin Doyle has not been informed about Attendance Allowance.
Margaret would need assistance with her hand to complete the Attendance Allowance form.
Kevin Doyle will help Margaret complete the Attendance Allowance form.
If the council arranges ongoing care, a financial assessment will determine whether Margaret would need to contribute financially.
Margaret may have to contribute financially to care, depending on income and savings.
The house is not counted in financial assessments for care at home.
Margaret stated she would prefer to pay a small amount and stay in her current home rather than move.

Margaret expressed concern about being frightened of falling and of the kitchen environment.
Margaret said she would like to cook a proper dinner now and then, such as mince and potatoes.
Margaret wants to see her roses (Frank's roses) grow and be well enough to go outside and look at them in summer.
Since the fall on 3rd March and two prior falls, Margaret finds it very hard to wash properly, especially bathing and hair, and dressing takes up to an hour and wears her out.
Margaret is unable to prepare proper meals and has lost nearly a stone in weight.
Margaret has missed some of her tablets.
Margaret is on her own a lot and feels lonely and more low than usual.
The falls and related difficulties are having a significant impact on Margaret's wellbeing, physical health, safety, mood, and ability to see people.
Margaret is likely to meet eligibility criteria for support, though confirmation requires agreement and is not yet certain.
The proposed support is reablement – short-term, free for up to six weeks, involving carers visiting to help with washing, dressing, tablets, and meals.
Reablement visits are proposed for morning (washing, dressing, tablets) and teatime (meal support), initially every day, tapering as confidence improves.
Reablement is not yet agreed and requires approval from the social worker’s manager.
Margaret does not want carers to be 'bossy' in her kitchen.
The social worker will include a note in the reablement request to ensure carers are not bossy.
